content.text: Hall with four great iwan openings.
Solid core inside the hall to carry the dome, then roof slab.
The dome is far too small for a Taj. Raising a taller drum around it and a proper big onion dome.
Four domed kiosks on the hall roof corners.
Dark recessed voids inside each iwan, then projecting arched pishtaq frames.
Crowning the pishtaqs: cornice plates that tie the frames into the hall, then a raised parapet.
Adding a sloped shoulder where the dome meets the drum.
Marble tile borders on both terrace steps.
Tiles landed on the minaret balconies — locating the strays.
Rebuilding the crown as a true onion bulb — waisted then bulged.
Tiling the hall roof terrace around the drum and kiosks.
